answer: In decentralized multi-agent networks, cryptographic proof of unique personhood prevents malicious entities from generating infinite fake identities. To deter resource-less nodes that might wander through the system, networks implement staking protocols requiring collateral, such as locked tokens or scarce computational resources akin to physical copper wiring in hardware. This economic cost creates a defensive spiral: as an attacker attempts to spawn fraudulent agents, the capital expenditure scales linearly or exponentially, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks economically unprofitable.
